datasets.name: USGS landslide inventory
datasets.verbatim: For example, in the U.S., the U.S. Geological Survey (USGS) maintains a database of landslide reports with approximate locations and times, but no images (https://doi.org/10.5066/P9E2A37P).

datasets.name: Google Earth satellite imagery
datasets.verbatim: Google Earth was used as the data source for the present study, which provides historical archives for multiple high-resolution aerial and satellite imagery.

methods.name: Task-Specific Model Updates (TSMU)
methods.summary: A continual learning semantic segmentation framework that uses a shared encoder and ecoregion-specific decoders. It employs incremental freeze training and joint fine-tuning with knowledge distillation to learn new tasks without catastrophic forgetting of old tasks.
methods.verbatim: Our dataset and code will be made publicly accessible upon acceptance in our GitHub repository at https://github.com/deepLDB/landslide-detection.

reproducibility_assessment: The landslide inventory is referenced and linked via a DOI, and the Google Earth imagery is accessible as a public resource. The custom code is provided via a persistent GitHub repository link.
